errors.evidence: The chart contains eight distinct lines (Eurozone + 7 countries), not seven.
The list of series and their visual representations omits Frankreich (France), which is represented by a light blue solid line.

errors.text_span: steigt kontinuierlich bis auf etwa 160 % im Jahr 2009
errors.evidence: The value for Greece in 2009 is approximately 125%, not 160%. It reaches 160% later, around 2011.

errors.text_span: erreicht einen Höhepunkt von etwa 200 % im Jahr 2011
errors.evidence: The peak of over 200% for Greece occurs around the year 2020, not 2011. In 2011, the value is approximately 175%.
The line for Italy does not remain stable; it shows a clear decreasing trend from about 118% in 1995 to about 105% in 2007.
This is an over-generalization for the period 2015-2025. The value for Italy peaks significantly higher, at around 155% in 2020, before falling back to around 140%.
The line for Spain (Spanien) begins at approximately 60% in 1995, not 50%.

errors.text_span: erreicht einen Höhepunkt von etwa 100 % im Jahr 2015 und stabilisiert sich bei etwa 100 % bis 2025
errors.evidence: This description is incorrect. Spain's debt ratio reaches 100% around 2014, but its actual peak in the depicted period is much higher, at approximately 120% in 2020. After 2020, it decreases to about 110% by 2025, not stabilizing at 100%.
The line for Ireland (Irland) begins at approximately 80% in 1995, not 60%.
The value for Ireland sinks to approximately 30% in 2005, not 40%.
The value for Ireland in 2015 is approximately 90%, not 70%.
The description incorrectly states that Germany's (Deutschland) debt ratio sinks until 2005. The chart shows it rising from ~60% in 2002 to ~68% in 2005.

errors.text_span: steigt leicht auf etwa 50 % im Jahr 2009
errors.evidence: The value for Germany in 2009 is approximately 75%, not 50%.
The value for Germany in 2015 is approximately 70%, not 45%.

This range is completely incorrect for the period after 2015. Germany's debt ratio is around 70% in 2015, drops to ~60% in 2019, jumps back to ~70% in 2020, and ends at ~60% in 2025. It is never in the 50-55% range during this time.
The line for France (Frankreich) does not remain stable; it shows a continuous upward trend, rising from ~68% in 2005 to ~85% in 2011.
This is an over-generalization and an understatement. The value for France rises to approximately 115% by 2020 and remains near that level, not 100%.

errors.text_span: Die Linie für die Eurozone beginnt bei etwa 60 % im Jahr 1995, sinkt bis etwa 50 % im Jahr 2005, steigt leicht bis etwa 60 % im Jahr 2009, fällt auf etwa 55 % im Jahr 2015 und bleibt bis 2025 bei etwa 60–65 %.
errors.evidence: Nearly all numerical values and trends described for the Eurozone are incorrect. It starts at ~72% (not 60%), sinks to ~65% (not 50%), rises to ~78% in 2009 (not 60%), is at ~92% in 2015 (not 55%), and its value from 2015-2025 is between ~90-100% (not 60-65%).
The value for Belgium (Belgien) in 2005 is approximately 95%, not 100%.
The line for Belgium does not remain stable from 2005 to 2015. It shows a clear increasing trend from ~85% in 2007 to over 105% by 2014.
